title: Specifications & Acceptance Criteria
description: Convert intent into precise, testable requirements that guide both AI implementation and human review.

lessons.title: Write behavior before implementation
lessons.principle: A specification should describe what the system must do before prescribing internal code.
lessons.practice: Lead with observable behavior, then add implementation constraints only when they matter.

lessons.title: Use testable language
lessons.principle: Words like fast, intuitive, robust, and secure are incomplete without measurable conditions.
lessons.practice: Translate adjectives into thresholds, scenarios, or explicit checks.

lessons.title: Separate functional and nonfunctional requirements
lessons.principle: Correct behavior and quality attributes require different validation.
lessons.practice: List functionality separately from performance, security, accessibility, reliability, and maintainability.

lessons.title: Use Given-When-Then for scenarios
lessons.principle: Scenario structure makes preconditions, actions, and expected outcomes explicit.
lessons.practice: Write critical acceptance cases as Given context, When action, Then observable result.

lessons.title: Specify negative requirements
lessons.principle: Knowing what must never happen prevents unsafe defaults.
lessons.practice: Include forbidden states, unauthorized actions, data leaks, duplicate side effects, and destructive behavior.

lessons.title: Define validation rules
lessons.principle: Inputs need authoritative shape and business constraints.
lessons.practice: Document required fields, formats, ranges, cross-field rules, and error responses.

lessons.title: Specify state transitions
lessons.principle: Stateful systems fail when transitions are implicit.
lessons.practice: List valid states, allowed transitions, guards, and what happens on interrupted transitions.

lessons.title: Describe API contracts
lessons.principle: Client-server ambiguity becomes integration defects.
lessons.practice: Specify methods, routes, schemas, authentication, status codes, idempotency, and error formats.

lessons.title: Describe database invariants
lessons.principle: Application logic is safer when persistent truths are explicit.
lessons.practice: State uniqueness, foreign-key, nullability, ownership, and consistency rules.

lessons.title: Define concurrency semantics
lessons.principle: Simultaneous actions can violate assumptions that pass single-user testing.
lessons.practice: Specify conflict handling, optimistic locking, idempotency, or serialization where needed.

lessons.title: Specify time behavior
lessons.principle: Dates, time zones, expiry, retries, and schedules are common sources of defects.
lessons.practice: State canonical time zones, clock assumptions, deadlines, and expiration semantics.

lessons.title: Specify file and media constraints
lessons.principle: Uploads need limits beyond a file picker.
lessons.practice: Define allowed types, size limits, validation, storage behavior, access, and deletion.

lessons.title: Create accessibility acceptance criteria
lessons.principle: Accessibility cannot be inferred from visual similarity.
lessons.practice: Require keyboard operation, focus behavior, semantics, labels, contrast, and screen-reader expectations.

lessons.title: Create performance budgets
lessons.principle: Performance goals are more enforceable when tied to budgets.
lessons.practice: Set relevant latency, bundle, query, memory, or Core Web Vitals targets.

lessons.title: Specify observability requirements
lessons.principle: A feature that cannot be diagnosed is incomplete operationally.
lessons.practice: Define logs, metrics, traces, audit events, and correlation fields for important flows.

lessons.title: Specify security requirements
lessons.principle: Security needs concrete trust boundaries and controls.
lessons.practice: State authorization, secret handling, data classification, rate limits, and abuse cases.

lessons.title: Define rollback acceptance
lessons.principle: Deployability includes the ability to recover.
lessons.practice: Specify what can be rolled back safely and how data changes behave across versions.

lessons.title: Make completion evidence explicit
lessons.principle: A task can appear done while key checks were never run.
lessons.practice: List the commands, test suites, screenshots, or manual scenarios required as evidence.

lessons.title: Version changing specifications
lessons.principle: Requirements evolve and the code should not obscure which version it implements.
lessons.practice: Keep spec changes reviewable and connect implementation changes to the updated requirement.

lessons.title: Use the spec as the review rubric
lessons.principle: A specification has highest leverage when it controls verification.
lessons.practice: Review the final diff against every acceptance criterion and record exceptions explicitly.
